newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PLOCK REFINERY TO CUT FUEL PRODUCTION.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PLOCK REFINERY TO CUT FUEL PRODUCTION.

text.p: Poland's biggest Plock refinery will cut its fuel production as a result of a court ruling which revoked an excise tax break enjoyed by refineries on imported half-products, a Plock official said on Thursday.
Marek Mroczkowski, head of the refinery's financial department told Reuters the ruling of the Constitutional Tribunal would boost the price of the half products and force curbs on Plock's production.
"We will buy and process less half-products so the amount of fuel which we sell will also decrease," Mroczkowski said.
"It is difficult to say how deep the reduction will be...in our case several percent," he said.
He said lower petrol production at Plock could affect fuel prices in the country, because the missing domestic fuel would have to be made up for by more expensive imports.
Polish prices of domestically-produced fuel are controlled by the finance ministry, which is reluctant to raise them fearing its ambitious inflation targets could be joepardised.
Poland's second largest Gdansk refinery said the court's ruling would not affect its production because it did not use imported half-products.
"We do not import half products...so the Tribunal's ruling does not affect us," Gdansk refinery spokeswoman Ewa Sielicka said.

The Constitutional Tribunal on Tuesday ruled that an excise tax relief on imported half-products enjoyed by refineries under a finance ministry regulation of November 1995 was unconstitutional as it favoured some companies over others.
Poland's seven refineries supply 80 percent of the country's fuel needs.
